question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose this plugin-owned external verification capability as the supported way for plugins to contribute an allow decision to a Gateway-owned protected-tool approval?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally security-sensitive and adds a lasting public plugin SDK plus persisted lifecycle contract; tests can verify mechanics but cannot determine the repository’s long-term authorization and support commitment.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow external-verifier contract
options.body: Accept the RFC-shaped Gateway-owned deny/final-ledger model and merge after normal required checks complete.

options.title: Narrow the supported API further
options.body: Keep the core boundary but require a reduced plugin API or different persistence/lifecycle guarantee before accepting it.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose an alternative extension boundary for external HITL verification.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow external-verifier contract
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC-shaped Gateway-owned deny/final-ledger model and merge after normal required checks complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC-shaped proposal and the companion plugin implementation, making them the strongest available technical-routing candidate for maintainer discussion.
